newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFA bans former Barings executive.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFA bans former Barings executive.

text.p: Britain's Securities and Futures Authority(SFA) said on Tuesday it has removed former Barings head of treasury and risk Ian Hopkins from its register of directors for at least three years.

In addition, Hopkins has been ordered to pay 10,000 pounds towards the SFA's costs after an independent tribunal found that he was no longer a "fit and proper person" to be a director of an SFA-regulated City firm.
UK's SFA bans former Barings executive

Hopkins was ultimately responsible at Barings Investment Bank for funding the group's activities and provided funds to Barings' futures operation in Singapore where trader Nick Leeson ran up losses of 800 million pounds which led to the collapse of the bank in February 1995.

Hopkins, one of nine Barings executives to have been disciplined by the SFA, has always protested that he attempted to "blow the whistle" on irregularities in the Singapore operation but that other managers ignored his warnings.

But this interpretation of his role was rejected by SFA chairman Nick Durlacher who said, "The facts do not support this suggestion. An impartial tribunal has scrupulously considered all the available evidence and judged (he) did not "blow the whistle" with any clarity, force or urgency."

Durlacher added that the tribunal had found that Hopkins', who did not offer a defence against the allegations, actions "fell far short of the standards expected of a prudent man in such a senior position."
